extracted.intended_audience: NPR editorial staff (reporters, editors, producers, hosts, visual and data journalists), freelance editorial contributors, and other newsroom staff who shape editorial content
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational ethics and editorial standards that govern how NPR journalists should report, produce, and present news and cultural content; covers core principles (accuracy, fairness, independence, etc.), applicability, and how principles should be balanced in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Our Mission
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of NPR, in partnership with its member stations, is to create a more informed public, one challenged and invigorated by a deeper understanding and appreciation of events, ideas, and culture within the United States and across the globe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To this end, NPR reports, produces, acquires and distributes news, information and other content that meet the highest standards of public service in journalism and cultural expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Our Guiding Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: NPR is, at its core, a news organization. Our work ... aspires to the heights of public service. We take seriously our democratic role as watchdogs, holding the powerful accountable as we hold ourselves to the core principles of honesty, integrity, independence, accuracy, contextual truth, transparency, respect and fairness for the people we serve and the people we cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truth requires the active pursuit of a diversity of voices, especially those most at risk of being left out. The handbook is intended not as a prescriptive list of do's and don'ts but as a foundation upon which staff should consider these often-competing principles and exercise judgment in deciding how to best represent NPR's core values and serve audiences with trusted journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability / Who is covered
rubrics_metrics.description: All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff are defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes leadership, managers, reporters, editors, newscasters, producers, visual journalists, data journalists, hosts and interns across News and Programming divisions, freelance editorial contributors and NPR events and promotions staff who shape editorially focused content. Non-editorial staff should follow NPR's Code of Conduct; administrative/support staff not involved in content decisions are not bound by this handbook. Contributors should adhere to the same standards depending on type of content creator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our purpose is to pursue the truth. Diligent verification is critical. We take great care to ensure that statements of fact in our journalism are both correct and in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We rigorously challenge both the claims we encounter and the assumptions we bring. We devote resources and skills to presenting the fullest version of the truth we can deliver, placing highest value on information gathered and verified ourselves. Subtopics listed: Accuracy in our reporting; Using information from non-NPR sources; Accuracy online; Accuracy in visual journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: To tell the truest story possible, it is essential that we treat those we interview and report on with scrupulous fairness, guided by a spirit of professionalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We make every effort to gather responses from those who are subjects of criticism or unfavorable allegations. Edited material should be faithful to interviewees' meaning. In controversial matters, strive to consider the strongest arguments on all sides and deliver both nuance and clarity. Goal is truth, not appearance of balance. Subtopics listed: Fairness in presenting the news; Fairness in reporting and interviewing; Fairness to colleagues; Fair use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: We do our best to report thoroughly and tell stories comprehensively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize limits of time/space but avoid errors of omission and partial truths which damage credibility. Stories delivered without sufficient context are incomplete. Include diverse voices reflecting society and divergent views that contribute to informed debate. When we can't deliver all answers, explain what we don't yet know and work to fill gaps. Subtopics listed: Telling the full story; Completeness in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists who conduct themselves honestly prove themselves worthy of trust. In the course of our work, we are genuine and candid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute information clearly, avoid hyperbole and sensational conjecture. Hypotheticals must be revealed; do not mix fiction with news reporting. Edit and present information honestly without deception; identify ourselves as NPR journalists when reporting. Only in rare, public-safety cases might identity be disguised, and such steps require rigorous deliberation and full disclosure afterwards. Subtopics listed: Honesty in reporting and interviewing; Honesty in presenting information; Honesty in visual journalism; Honesty online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: To secure the public's trust, we must make it clear that our primary allegiance is to the public. Any personal or professional interests that conflict with that allegiance, whether in appearance or reality, risk compromising our credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be vigilant in disclosing circumstances where loyalties may be divided, including interests of spouses and family, and recuse when necessary. Do not skew reports for personal gain, NPR's bottom line, or to please funders. Editorial decisions are made by journalists, not funders. Subtopics listed: Conflicts of interest; Interacting with funders; Owning our news agenda; Outside work; Paying our own way; Working for NPR while keeping the public first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Our experiences and perspectives are valuable assets to our journalism. We enjoy the right to robust personal lives, yet we accept some unique professional obligations and limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because our words and actions can damage public opinion of NPR, we comport ourselves in ways that honor professional impartiality. We may have opinions but the public deserves factual reporting and informed analysis without our opinions unduly influencing coverage. Aggressively challenge our own perspectives and pursue diverse range of others to present truth as completely as possible. Subtopics listed: Impartiality in our personal lives; Impartiality in our journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: To inspire confidence in our journalism, it is critical that we give the public the tools to evaluate our work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveal as much as practically possible about how we discover and verify facts. Make decision-making clear to the public, especially when wrestling with tough choices. Disclose relationships with partners or funders that might appear to influence coverage. Subtopics listed: Revealing our process; Anonymous sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: We take full responsibility for our work, so we must always be ready and willing to answer for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listen to the public; welcome questions and criticisms and respond as able. Mistakes will be corrected forthrightly, with reflection and learning. Subtopics listed: Corrections; Interacting with the public; Accountability online; Legal accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect
rubrics_metrics.description: Everyone affected by our journalism deserves to be treated with decency and compassion. We are civil in our actions and words, avoiding arrogance and hubris.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listen to others, ask tough questions to seek answers not confrontation. Be sensitive to cultural differences, minimize undue harm, take special care with those who are vulnerable or suffering, and be mindful of privacy while fulfilling journalistic obligations. Subtopics listed: Respect for sources and subjects of coverage; Respect in sensitive circumstances; Respect for our audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Our journalism is most valuable when we marry important truths with engaging narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take pride in craftsmanship of storytelling and quality of words, sounds, and images used to illuminate the world. Edit to add impact and clarity — never to slant or distort. Avoid sensationalism overshadowing significance; aspire to stories that rise above maudlin or mundane sentimentality. Subtopics listed: Excellence in storytelling; Excellence in news judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Putting Principles Into Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: We will fulfill the high standard we owe the public if we hold true to our principles. Doing so requires that we embrace complexity and continually think through difficult decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles often reinforce but also tension with one another; balance them against one another, striving to honor the mission. The statement is intended to provoke discussion and deliberation — to test and strengthen the moral compass that guides daily work. Also includes practical sections and ongoing editorial guidance (e.g., Standards & Practices notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial guidance and special sections (practical topic areas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards & Practices Editor Tony Cavin writes occasional notes about issues journalists encounter and how NPR handles them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special sections and topical guidance referenced include: Anonymous sourcing; Attribution; Diversity; Generative artificial intelligence; Social Media; Speaking Appearances; Visual journalism; and platform-specific items (Facebook, Flipboard). These indicate areas where the handbook provides or links to more specific procedural guidance.
